transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess... the main thing is I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I’ll start trying to explain something simple from an overnight shift, and then suddenly I’m talking about soccer, and then paint colors, and then patient charts, and I can see people’s faces changing like they’re trying to follow me but they can’t.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I know I’m trying to say something that makes sense, but it comes out all tangled. I’ll be halfway through a sentence and then another thought cuts in, and I follow that one, and then I don’t even know how I got there. That’s kind of what brought me in.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your head by someone else, or like they're being taken out, or even that other people can hear your thoughts?

I don’t know if it’s exactly like someone putting thoughts in my head, no… not in that way. It’s more like I can tell there’s something going on around me, like at work. The supervisors keep changing my shifts, and people say, “Oh, that’s just staffing, we’re short,” or “Everybody’s schedule is messy,” but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels too specific.

Like I’ll get moved to certain shifts, or placed where the cameras have a better view, and I know the unit has cameras anyway, I’m not saying cameras are unusual there, but it feels like they’re using them to watch me specifically. Like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up. And when I try to explain that, people act like I’m making connections that aren’t there, but I’m pretty sure I’m not. It’s hard to ignore when the shifts change and then I feel like I’m being watched more closely.

So… not that people can hear my thoughts, exactly. More that they’re watching me and arranging things around me because they think something is wrong with me.
Do you ever feel like your actions, thoughts, or feelings are being controlled by something or someone outside of yourself?

Controlled… I don’t know if I’d say it like my hands are being moved or anything like that. I’m not saying somebody has a remote control over me. But it does feel like people are arranging things around me, if that counts.

Like with my supervisors at work — I’m pretty sure they’re changing my shifts on purpose and putting me in certain places where the unit cameras can see me better. People keep telling me it’s just staffing shortages, or that everyone’s schedule is getting moved around, but it doesn’t feel like “everyone” when it keeps happening in ways that line up with me. It feels like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to do something wrong.

So not controlled inside my head, exactly. More like outside things are being controlled around me, and I’m the reason for it. And I know that probably sounds like I’m reading too much into it, but when it keeps happening, it’s hard to believe it’s just random.
Do you ever feel like things that are happening around you — like events, people’s actions, or even things on TV or the news — are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning just for you?

Yeah… I mean, not really with TV or the news, I don’t think. It’s more at work. That’s where it feels like things are… aimed at me, I guess.

Like the shift changes. People keep saying it’s staffing shortages, or that everybody’s schedule is getting shuffled around, and I know that happens. I’m not stupid, I know units get short and people get moved. But the way it happens to me feels too specific. Like I’ll get put on certain shifts, or moved around to places where the cameras have a better view, and then it feels like the supervisors are watching me through the unit cameras.

And not just in the normal way cameras are there for everyone. It feels like they’re checking me, like watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up. I know people tell me I’m overthinking it, but it doesn’t feel like overthinking when it keeps lining up like that. It feels like the whole schedule is being arranged around me for a reason.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like things people do, things you see, or events happening around you are meant for you or have a special meaning for you specifically?

Outside of work… not really in the same way. Like I don’t usually watch TV and think the news is talking to me or something. It’s mostly tied to work, because that’s where the pattern is. That’s where the shift changes happen, and where the cameras are, and where the supervisors have a reason to be watching.

I know people keep saying it’s staffing shortages, and I get that staffing can be bad, I’m not saying schedules never change. But with me it feels too exact. Like they move me to a certain shift or put me somewhere that has a better camera angle, and then I’m just aware the whole time that they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up.

So outside of work, no, I don’t think everything has a special meaning for me. But at work, yes, absolutely. It feels directed at me. It doesn’t feel random.
Do you ever feel like things people say or do in public — like strangers talking, things written online, or even music lyrics — are sending you a hidden message or talking directly to you?

Not really with strangers or music lyrics or online stuff. I don’t usually hear a song and think it’s secretly about me, or see something online and feel like it’s a message. That’s not really how it happens for me.

It’s more specific than that. It’s at work, with the supervisors and the schedule and the cameras. Like, I’m sure they’ve changed my shifts around on purpose, and then put me in places where the unit cameras can watch me better. People keep telling me it’s just staffing shortages, like “everybody’s getting moved around,” but it doesn’t feel like that when it keeps happening to me in ways that line up too perfectly.

And then once I’m there, I can’t stop thinking they’re watching through the cameras to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to do something wrong. Not just normal camera watching — I know cameras are there anyway — but watching me specifically. So, hidden messages from strangers, no… but people doing things in a way that’s meant for me, yeah, that part I do feel pretty strongly at work.
Have you ever felt like random events or things people say in everyday life — like conversations, signs, or things happening around you — have a hidden meaning or are connected to you in some way?

Yeah… I mean, in everyday life, not so much like signs on the street or strangers talking near me. I don’t usually think a random conversation at a store is about me or anything like that.

But at work, I do feel like things are connected to me in a way people keep trying to explain away. Like the shift changes. They’ll say it’s just staffing shortages, or that everyone is getting moved because the unit is short, and I understand that on one level. I know schedules change. But with mine, it feels too targeted. Like supervisors are changing my shifts on purpose and putting me in certain spots where the unit cameras can see me better.

And then once I notice that, it’s hard not to see the whole thing as planned. Like they’re watching me through the cameras to see if I’m unsafe, or if I’m going to do something wrong. Not just general camera monitoring — I mean watching me specifically. People tell me I’m making connections that aren’t there, but it doesn’t feel random when it keeps happening in that exact way. So if you mean random everyday stuff, no, not really. But at work, yeah, it feels like it’s definitely connected to me.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like things people do, things you see, or events happening around you are meant for you or have a special meaning for you specifically?

Outside of work, not really… I mean, I don’t walk around thinking every little thing is about me. Like if someone laughs in a store or I see something on TV, I don’t usually take it as a sign or a message for me specifically.

It’s more that at work it feels very directed. I know I’ve said that, but that’s where it happens. The supervisors changing my shifts, moving me around, putting me in places where the cameras can see better… people keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, like it’s normal and everyone gets moved, but it doesn’t feel normal when it keeps lining up with me like that.

And then I’m there on the unit and I’m aware of the cameras the whole time, like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up. Not just watching the unit in general — watching me. So outside of work, no, not really special meanings like that. But at work, yes, it feels meant for me.
Outside of the situations at work, do you ever feel like your thoughts or actions are being directly controlled by something outside of yourself, like a person, device, or force?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, outside of work, I don’t really feel like something is controlling my body or making me do things like I’m a puppet or something. My thoughts are my thoughts, even when I get stuck on them or stressed about them.

Like, I might second-guess myself a lot, and I might worry about why something happened, but I don’t feel like a device or a person or some force is directly moving me or putting actions into me. That’s not really how it feels. It’s more like I’m reacting to things and thinking too much about them, not like I’ve lost control of myself.

So… no, not that I’ve noticed.

Outside of work, have you ever felt like things happening around you — like people’s actions, events, or even things you see or hear — are directly related to you or have a special personal meaning, even if others don’t see the connection?

Outside of work… no, not really in the way you’re saying. I don’t usually feel like random things I see or hear are messages for me, or like strangers’ actions have some special meaning connected to me.

It’s mostly the work situation that feels like that, and I know I keep coming back to it, but that’s because that’s where it actually happens. Like with the supervisors changing my shifts, they’ll say it’s staffing shortages or that everyone gets moved around, but I’m sure it’s more than that with me. It feels like they’re putting me in certain places on purpose, where the unit cameras can see me better, and then watching me to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to do something wrong.

So if you mean outside of work, no, I don’t really have that. But at work, yeah, it feels directly related to me, even when other people say I’m reading into it.
Do you ever feel like people at work are sending you secret messages or communicating about you through subtle actions, even if others wouldn't notice it?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it “secret messages” like codes or anything like that, but at work it does feel like people are communicating about me without saying it straight out.

Like when my shifts get changed or I get moved to a different part of the unit, they’ll say it’s because of staffing shortages or because everyone has to rotate, but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like the supervisors are arranging it around me specifically. Like they’re putting me in certain spots where the cameras have a better view, and then watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up.

And other people might not notice it because they just see a schedule change or someone being moved around, but when it keeps happening to me, and it lines up with where the cameras are, it feels pretty clear. I feel like they know what they’re doing, even if they don’t say it out loud. So not exactly secret messages, but subtle actions, yeah. That’s what it feels like.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like things people do, things you see, or events happening around you are meant for you or have a special meaning for you specifically?

Outside of work… no, I don’t really feel that way. Like if I’m walking around somewhere or watching something or someone says something near me, I don’t usually think it’s meant for me or has some special meaning aimed at me. I don’t really get that feeling out in regular places.

It’s more at work that it happens, and I know I keep separating it like that, but that’s because that’s honestly how it feels. At work, when they change my shifts or move me around the unit, they’ll tell me it’s just staffing shortages or that everybody gets moved sometimes, but I don’t believe that’s all it is. I’m sure the supervisors are changing things with me in mind. Like they’re putting me in certain areas where the unit cameras can see me better, and then watching me to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to do something wrong.

So outside of work, not really. But at work, yes, those things feel like they’re about me specifically, even when other people say I’m reading too much into it.
Outside of work, have you ever felt like things people do or events happening around you have a hidden connection to you, even if they don’t seem related to others?

Outside of work, no… I don’t really get that feeling. Like if somebody at a store looks at me a certain way, or if there’s some random thing happening around me, I don’t usually think it’s connected to me or meant for me. I can usually just let that be whatever it is.

But at work, it’s different, and that’s where I keep getting stuck on it. I know I’ve said it a few times, but it’s not like I’m trying to make everything about me everywhere. It’s specifically there. When the supervisors change my shifts or move me to different parts of the unit, they’ll say it’s because of staffing shortages or because people get moved around all the time, but I’m sure there’s more to it than that.

It feels like they’re choosing certain spots for me on purpose, especially where the unit cameras can see me better. Like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up. Other people act like I’m overthinking it, but when it keeps happening, it’s hard for me to believe it’s just random scheduling. So outside of work, not really. At work, yes, it feels connected to me.
Do you ever feel like people outside of work, like friends, family, or strangers, are also acting in ways that seem directed at you or have a hidden meaning for you?

Not really with friends or family or strangers, no. I mean, I can get uncomfortable around people sometimes, but I don’t usually think random people outside of work are doing things with some hidden meaning for me.

It’s mostly the work thing. That’s where it feels directed at me. Like the supervisors changing my shifts or moving me around the unit — they’ll tell me it’s just staffing shortages, or that everybody has to rotate, or whatever explanation they give, but I don’t believe that’s the whole reason. It feels like they’re doing it on purpose with me specifically in mind.

Especially when I end up in spots where the unit cameras can see me better. Then I start thinking, okay, they’re watching me to see if I’m unsafe, or if I’m going to mess something up. And people act like I’m making connections that aren’t there, but to me it doesn’t feel like a coincidence when it keeps happening.

So outside of work, no, not really. But at work, yes — that’s where I feel like people are acting in ways that are aimed at me, even if they don’t come out and say it.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like something — even something small or indirect — is secretly connected to you, even if it doesn’t seem obvious to others?

Outside of work… no, not really. I know that probably sounds like I’m being really specific about it, but I don’t walk around thinking every little thing is secretly connected to me. Like, if something small happens outside, or someone says something nearby, I don’t usually take it as a sign or anything like that.

It’s just work where it feels different. That’s the part I can’t really shake. With the supervisors, when they change my shifts or move me around, they always have an explanation ready — staffing shortages, someone called out, everybody gets moved around, that kind of thing. But I’m sure they’re changing mine on purpose. It feels too specific, like they’re placing me where the unit cameras can see me better.

And then I start thinking they’re watching me to see if I’m unsafe, or if I’m going to do something wrong. People tell me it’s just normal scheduling stuff, but it doesn’t feel normal to me. So outside of work, no, I don’t really feel that hidden connection. At work, yes, I do.

When you're at work and you feel like things are being arranged around you, do you believe that this is happening because someone is deliberately trying to harm you or because you have done something wrong?

I don’t know if I’d say they’re trying to harm me exactly, like physically hurt me or anything like that. It’s more like… they think I’ve done something wrong, or they think I’m going to do something wrong, and they’re setting things up to catch it.

When they change my shifts or move me to different parts of the unit, I’m sure it’s not just staffing. They always say it’s staffing shortages or coverage or whatever, but I don’t really believe that’s the whole reason. It feels deliberate. Like they’re putting me in certain spots where the cameras can see me better, and then they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I mess up.

So, yeah, I guess it feels like I’m being treated like I did something wrong, even if nobody says it straight to me. That’s what bothers me so much — they act like it’s normal scheduling, but it feels like there’s a reason they’re watching me.
Outside of work, have you ever felt like people were acting against you, plotting against you, or treating you unfairly for reasons that others wouldn't understand or agree with?

Outside of work, no… I don’t really feel like people are plotting against me or treating me unfairly in some secret way. Like, I don’t usually think strangers or family or people outside are against me like that.

It’s more at work, and I know I keep coming back to that, but that’s where it feels real to me. With the supervisors, when my shifts get changed or they move me around the unit, they say it’s because of staffing shortages or coverage or everyone rotating, but I don’t believe that’s all it is. I’m sure they’re changing things around with me in mind.

And when I end up in places where the cameras can see me better, it feels like they’re watching me — like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up. Other people don’t seem to agree with me about it, and they act like I’m reading too much into it, but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels deliberate.
Have you ever experienced situations outside of work where you felt like events or people’s actions were specifically targeted at you, even if they seemed normal to others?

Outside of work, not really, no. I mean, I try to think about it carefully because I know it probably sounds like I’m saying, “Only at work,” over and over, but that’s honestly how it is for me.

Like if I’m at the store or walking somewhere, I don’t usually feel like people are arranging things around me or that normal stuff is secretly aimed at me. I don’t think every person looking at their phone is talking about me or anything like that. It’s not like that all the time in every place.

But at work, it’s different. That’s where I’m sure something is going on. The supervisors keep changing my shifts or moving me around, and they’ll say it’s just staffing shortages or that everyone gets moved depending on coverage, but it doesn’t feel like that to me. It feels like they’re doing it with me specifically in mind, like putting me where the unit cameras can watch me more clearly.

And when I say that, people act like I’m making too much out of normal scheduling, but I don’t think I am. It feels deliberate. Like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up. So outside of work, no, I haven’t really had that. It’s really centered on work and the cameras and the shift changes.

At work, when you feel things are being arranged around you, do you believe that these events are happening because you are the focus of other people's attention or that things are being done specifically to communicate something to you?

Yeah… I think it’s more that I’m the focus of their attention, if that makes sense. Like I don’t think they’re trying to send me a message with the schedule, like some kind of code or hidden meaning. It’s not like, “This shift means this” or “this assignment means that.” It’s more like the changes are being made because of me.

When my shifts get changed, or they move me to another part of the unit, I can’t see it as just random staffing stuff. They say it’s shortages or coverage, and I know that’s what they tell everyone, but with me it feels different. I feel sure the supervisors are moving me around on purpose so they can watch me better through the unit cameras. Like they’re trying to see if I’m unsafe, or if I’m going to make a mistake, or if I’m doing something wrong.

So I guess, yes, I feel like I’m the focus. Not that they’re communicating something to me exactly, but that they’re arranging things around me and watching me. And that’s why it’s hard for me to just accept it when people say, “No, it’s just staffing.” Because it doesn’t feel like just staffing to me.
Outside of work, have you ever had any experiences where you felt like you were being watched, followed, or targeted by others in any way?

Outside of work, no… not really. I don’t have that feeling walking down the street or going to the store, like somebody is following me or strangers are watching me. I don’t usually think people outside are targeting me.

It’s mainly at work where that feeling happens, and it’s pretty strong there. Like I keep saying, with the shift changes and being moved around the unit, they tell me it’s just staffing shortages or coverage, but I don’t believe that’s the whole reason. I’m sure the supervisors are changing things with me in mind.

And the cameras make it worse, because when they move me to certain areas, it feels like they’re putting me where they can see me better. Like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe, or if I’m going to mess up. Other people say I’m reading into it, but it doesn’t feel that way to me. It feels like it’s specifically about me at work.

inference_history.note: This turn adds concern for thought insertion/broadcasting and referential delusions (though the patient denies classic thought insertion). The patient describes a belief that others are monitoring and manipulating their environment based on suspicions about their behavior, consistent with delusional ideation. This rules out F21 (acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia), F29 (unspecified psychosis), and F20.4-F20.5 (simple schizophrenia and unspecified schizophrenia, which are less likely at this point). The thought form disturbance and delusional framework raise strong concern for schizophrenia spectrum disorders (F20.x, F25.x) and delusional disorder (F22), as well as schizotypal (F23.2) and possibly other psychotic disorders (F28).

The patient denies thought insertion, thought withdrawal, and thought broadcasting, which reduces likelihood of schizophrenia (F20.0, F20.1, F20.2, F20.3). The focus on being observed and shift changes being specifically directed at them supports delusional themes, narrowing more toward delusional disorder or other persistent delusional disorders (F22, F23.x).
